title: Ketamine or Etomidate for Tracheal Intubation of Critically Ill Adults
shortTitle: RSI: ketamine did not improve survival and increased cardiovascular collapse
authors: RSI Investigators and the Pragmatic Critical Care Research Group
summary: This multicenter trial assigned 2,365 critically ill adults undergoing intubation to ketamine or etomidate. In-hospital mortality by day 28 was similar, while cardiovascular collapse during intubation occurred more often with ketamine.
whyItMatters: Do not assume ketamine protects hemodynamics or improves survival compared with etomidate during emergency intubation. Plan blood-pressure support whichever induction agent is chosen.
limitations: The trial was unblinded and included both ED and ICU patients. The mortality confidence interval includes clinically meaningful differences in either direction.
population: Critically ill adults undergoing intubation at 14 US ED/ICU sites.
findings: Mortality: 28.1% versus 29.1%; adjusted risk difference -0.8 percentage points (95% CI -4.5 to 2.9).
Cardiovascular collapse: 22.1% versus 17.0%; risk difference 5.1 percentage points (95% CI 1.9 to 8.3).
evidenceNotes: Publisher and PubMed indexed abstracts reviewed. Legal author manuscript is identified as PMC12711137, but its full text was not reviewed. Publisher confirms December 9 online date; April 2026 is the print issue. Direct journal/PubMed opens encountered access challenges.
